newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW -Monsanto sees 20 pct growth for Roundup.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW -Monsanto sees 20 pct growth for Roundup.

text.p: Monsanto Co said its flagship Roundup herbicide remains on track to show about 20 percent growth in global sales in 1997, despite a cold spring that cut early demand in the United States.

"Roundup is still having a very good year," Nicholas Filippello, the company's chief economist, said Tuesday in an interview. "For the first half of the year...global volumes for Roundup are still growing right on track with long-term expected trends" of about 20 percent a year globally.
Analysts estimate Roundup annual sales at $2.5 billion.
"Roundup carries the day and will continue to carry the day," Merrill Lynch analyst Doug Groh said.
Monsanto said Roundup volumes for the second quarter and the first half were up significantly from year-ago periods.

Earlier, Monsanto reported second quarter earnings of $324.0 million or $0.54 a share in the second quarter after a a charge of $72 million or $0.12 a share to write off in-process research and development related to its Calgene Inc acquisition.

Filippello said Monsanto's pending acquisition of Holden's Foundation Seeds Inc will result in a charge for in-process research and development that likely will be bigger than its year-to-date writeoffs of $173 million.
He noted that in-process research write-offs are accounting measures only and have no impact on cash earnings.
Excluding the writeoff, St. Louis-based Monsanto had record second-quarter earnings of $396 million or $0.66 a share, up from $365 million or $0.62 a share a year ago.
Filippello said results met analysts' expectations, which had been reduced "a little bit" previously due to the cold spring in the United States.
"The weather was colder than expected and that translated to reduced weed growth, so farmers didn't have to apply as much Roundup as expected," Natwest Securities analyst Mark Wiltamuth said.
Wiltamuth added that significant plantings of new genetically altered crops that tolerate the use of Roundup, such as Roundup Ready soybeans, will boost use of the herbicide in the third quarter.

Monsanto's second-quarter results also included lower earnings for pharmaceuticals, which dropped to $9 million from $36 million a year ago. Pharmaceutical income was hurt by accelerated development spending.
Monsanto said five products, including an arthritis treatment called celecoxib, are in Phase III clinical trials.
Filippello said Monsanto's G.D. Searle pharmaceutical unit funds some of its research expenses with payments made under co-development alliances.
These payments will be a "very significant portion of Searle's income in the second half" of the year, with payments likely weighted more toward the fourth quarter, he added.
